title: Lighthouse elevation playbook & SLA pathways
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, execution-focused playbook for Customer Success (Lighthouse accounts) to: 1) identify candidates for Dedicated capacity, Private deployment, or Premium SLA upgrades; 2) run a QBR-driven business case and renewal conversation; 3) coordinate technical validation and migration planning across Solutions, Eng, and Product.

When to use (quick filters):
- Quarterly spend > $12k/month and unpredictable latency spikes
- Data-sensitivity / compliance ask that cannot be met by hosted-only options
- Customer requests SLA or dedicated throughput guarantees
- Repeated production incidents where fallback to hosted is insufficient

Core objectives for each engagement:
- Reduce customer-perceived latency by X% (goal: 30%)
- Improve request/second capacity predictability (SLO target slot)
- Convert to a committed contract or pilot that de-risks migration cost for both sides

QBR template (section prompts for slide deck):
- Exec snapshot: usage trend (tokens/day), cost/opportunity, key customer metrics (latency p95, errors)
- Business outcomes: top 3 product initiatives relying on inference; revenue or CAC impact
- Health signals: uptime, retried requests, KV cache hit rate (if available), example incidents last 90d
- Migration case: recommended path (Dedicated / Private / SLA add-on), expected improvement, high-level cost delta
- Ask + next steps: decision deadline, pilot scope, success criteria, required resources

Renewal tracker (use this in the QBR deck notes):
- Renewal window start: 90 days before term end
- Pilot decision target: 45 days before term end
- Pricing anchor: list current blended unit cost, proposed committed unit price, cap on overage
- Financial win-ladders: 10%, 20%, 35% discount tiers tied to committed monthly tokens or reserved GPUs

Technical validation checklist (solutions-engineering + serving-runtime):
- Baseline: capture 1 week of production traces (latency distribution, seq len distro)
- Model compatibility: confirm model weights + quantization path supported on target infra
- Performance sim: run representative load-generator for QPS target and 2x burst for 30m
- Data flow: record ingress/egress paths, PII/PIA flags, required audit logs and retention windows
- Fall-back plan: define downgrade model variants and traffic split for staged rollout
- Security: KMS integration, IP allowlist, VPC peering or private link path
- Ops hooks: metrics to add to console dashboard (token cost, billing label, rollout flag)

Sales / commercial play (scripts & negotiation tips):
- Anchor on predictability and measurable SLA outcomes rather than raw model access
- Offer a 30-day pilot with credits for infra if customer signs a 9–12 month reserved commit
- TCO calculator: show current hosted cost vs reserved Dedicated with conservative batching gains
- If privacy is primary: prioritize Private deployment + audit review; position as compliance-first path

Sample outreach (first QBR invite):
Subject: QBR + performance review — proposal to improve latency and reduce cost
Hi <Customer Exec/PO>,
We’d like to run a short QBR to review last quarter’s performance and walk through a proposed pilot that could reduce your p95 latency by ~30% and stabilize cost. Suggested agenda: 20m health review, 25m technical pilot scope, 10m contract/next steps. Are you available wk of <date>?

Internal action plan (SRE/Eng handoffs):
- Week 0: CS to collect traces + schedule architecture review (owner: Solutions Eng)
- Week 1–2: POC infra + performance sim (owner: serving-runtime eng)
- Week 3: Security and compliance checklist (owner: security eng)
- Week 4: Pilot kickoff — set SLOs, dashboard, escalation path

Risk matrix (quick):
- Migration cost > expectations -> mitigation: phased pilot + cap on pilot spend
- Model quality regression due to quantization -> mitigation: A/B tests + rollbacks
- Network/VPC complexity -> mitigation: run a staging VPC replica and pre-authorized peering checklist

Decision rubric (for renewals):
- Green: Pilot shows latency p95 improvement >= 20% and unit cost reduction >= 15% -> recommend commit to Dedicated or Private pilot conversion
- Amber: Partial improvement or missing security signoff -> extend pilot + targeted fixes, negotiate short-term SLA add-on
- Red: No measurable lift or model regressions -> deprioritize migration; consider cache/batching optimizations instead

Playbook TODOs (short list for next QBR cycle):
- [ ] Create one-pager TCO calculator template (owner: CS Ops)
- [ ] Add default dashboard view in Console for pilot customers (owner: Product/Console)
- [ ] Canonical pilot SOW template for Dedicated and Private (owner: Legal + Solutions)

Notes to self / fragments:
- Consider building a pre-approved 'pilot credit' SKU that reduces friction for engineering resources scheduling
- Keep a curated list of 3 model-variant fallbacks per architecture (gpt-style, mix of 7b/13b/70b)
- For noisy customers, proactively propose a phased ingress cap to protect shared capacity

References / links: CONFLUENCE:cs/lighthouse-elevation (detailed checklist), CS-4821 (renewal case notes), GH:redwood/cs-playbooks/pull/79 (pilot SOW template)
